title: [Bug]: structured output can sample unconstrained tokens when the draft hand-off goes stale (spec decode + async scheduling + PP)
body:
## Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ``` ```
## 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary The draft-token hand-off from the worker to the scheduler carries no identity: `DraftTokensHandler` holds a single slot that every `execute_model` overwrites. When a structured-output request's drafts are lost that way, its `-1` placeholders survive into `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask`, which then writes `_full_mask` — **every token in the vocabulary allowed** — at rows that are real sampling positions. The worker verifies the genuine drafts from its own GPU-resident copy, so acceptance can walk straight into those rows and emit up to `num_speculative_tokens` tokens with no grammar constraint at all. The failure is silent by construction: the mask fails **open**. When the emitted tokens happen to be grammar-legal the request is quietly corrupted and keeps generating from a poisoned context; when they are not, the request dies with ``` ERROR [backend_xgrammar.py] Failed to advance FSM for request for tokens . ERROR [scheduler.py] Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [30, 128825, ...] for request . Terminating request. ``` **This is latent on `main` today** — see "Reachability" below. It becomes live the moment a pipeline-parallel-capable drafter lands, which is why it seems worth fixing before that happens rather than after. All line numbers below are `main` @ `87b9b5b`. ### The chain **1. The scheduler installs `-1` placeholders for the next step's drafts.** `vllm/v1/core/sched/async_scheduler.py:42-44` ```python # Add placeholders for the new draft/spec tokens. # We will update the actual spec token ids in the worker process. request.spec_token_ids = self._spec_token_placeholders # [-1] * K ``` **2. They are back-filled from a single, unidentified slot.** The deferred-sampling branch (`vllm/v1/engine/core.py:678`, back-fill at `:736`) calls `take_draft_token_ids()`, which resolves to `DraftTokensHandler` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/utils.py:11`): ```python def set_draft_tokens(self, input_batch, draft_tokens) -> None: self.req_ids = input_batch.req_ids # :25 — overwritten every step self.num_draft_tokens = draft_tokens.shape[1] if not input_batch.has_structured_output_reqs: self.draft_tokens_np = None # and cleared by plain batches return ``` No step id, no batch id, no history. The slot is correct only when the batch that last reached the worker covers the same requests as the step being sampled. That holds at `pipeline_parallel_size == 1`, where `max_concurrent_batches` is 2 (`vllm/config/vllm.py:563`): the deferred branch pops one entry and blocks on it, and the slot ends up holding exactly the predecessor's drafts. Under pipeline parallelism it does not hold. `max_concurrent_batches` becomes `pp_size + 1`, and `next_decode_eligible_step = current_step + pp_size` (`async_scheduler.py:48`) alternates requests across microbatches, so the batch that wrote the slot is a *different request set* than the one being sampled. There is also a second, more direct path (`utils.py:48-51`): ```python else: # This case only happens when async scheduling is disabled. draft_token_ids = [[-1] * self.num_draft_tokens for _ in self.req_ids] ``` That comment is not accurate: the branch is taken whenever the last batch to reach `set_draft_tokens` had no structured-output requests, which a plain-only microbatch does routinely. **3. A surviving `-1` makes the bitmask fail open.** `vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py:301-306` ```python for i, token in enumerate(req_tokens): self._fill_bitmasks(((grammar, cumulative_index, apply_bitmask),)) # row i filled FIRST advance_grammar = apply_bitmask if token == -1: # :304 apply_bitmask = False # rows i+1.. get _full_mask advance_grammar = False ``` `_full_mask` is `torch.tensor(-1, dtype=torch.int32)` — 32 bits set (`:59`, applied at `:213`) — and `apply_grammar_bitmask` only writes `-inf` where a bit is **0**. "The mask could not be built" therefore renders as "every token is allowed". Note that row 0 is filled *before* `req_tokens[0]` is inspected, so it is always correct. Only rows `1..K-1` go permissive. **4. Meanwhile the model verifies the real drafts, not the `-1`s.** The `-1` exists only in the scheduler's copy. The worker builds `input_ids` from its own GPU-resident `req_states.draft_tokens` via `combine_sampled_and_draft_tokens`, so the rejection sampler verifies genuine draft tokens against rows whose mask allows everything. Accepting any of them emits a token the grammar never allowed. ### Reproduction on stock `main`, without a model `repro.py` below drives the two links directly. It needs a CUDA device (for the handler's copy stream) and the `gpt2` tokenizer; no model weights.
repro.py ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Reproduce the structured-output hole on stock vLLM main, without a model. The end-to-end symptom needs pipeline parallelism, and every draft head whose checkpoint is small enough to test with (Eagle3Llama, MiMoMTP, ...) refuses PP because it does not implement `SupportsPP`, while `create_draft_parallel_config` copies the target's pp_size verbatim. So drive the two links of the chain directly instead; together they are the whole bug. Link A `DraftTokensHandler` keeps ONE slot with no identity, so a batch that does not contain a request destroys that request's drafts. Link B the `-1` placeholders that therefore survive make `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask` emit `_full_mask` -- every token allowed -- at rows that are REAL sampling positions, because the worker verifies the genuine drafts from its own GPU-resident copy. Run with the stock venv: .venv/bin/python stock_unit_repro.py """ import sys from types import SimpleNamespace import numpy as np import torch from transformers import AutoTokenizer from vllm.config import StructuredOutputsConfig, VllmConfig from vllm.config.model import ModelConfig from vllm.config.speculative import SpeculativeConfig from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams, StructuredOutputsParams from vllm.v1.request import Request from vllm.v1.structured_output import StructuredOutputManager from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.utils import DraftTokensHandler TOKENIZER = "gpt2" K = 4 ok = True def report(name, holds, detail=""): """Each assertion states an observed fact about the current code. `yes` means the fact holds, which for the Link A/B facts means the bug is present.""" global ok ok = ok and holds print(f" [{'yes' if holds else 'NO '}] {name}{(' ' + detail) if detail else ''}") # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Link A: the single slot has no identity. # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- def link_a(): print("\nLink A -- DraftTokensHandler keeps one unidentified slot") dev = torch.device("cuda:0") handler = DraftTokensHandler(dev) # Only `req_ids` and `has_structured_output_reqs` are read off the batch. def batch(req_ids, structured): return SimpleNamespace( req_ids=list(req_ids), has_structured_output_reqs=structured ) drafts_a = torch.arange(1, 1 + 2 * K, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev).reshape(2, K) drafts_b = torch.arange(101, 101 + 2 * K, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev).reshape(2, K) # Batch A carries the structured-output request. handler.set_draft_tokens(batch(["gA", "pA"], True), drafts_a) got = handler.get_draft_tokens() report( "drafts for 'gA' are available right after its own batch", "gA" in got.req_ids, f"req_ids={got.req_ids}", ) # Another microbatch runs. Under PP this is the other half of the requests. handler.set_draft_tokens(batch(["gB", "pB"], True), drafts_b) got = handler.get_draft_tokens() report( "after another batch runs, 'gA' can no longer be found", "gA" not in got.req_ids, f"req_ids={got.req_ids} -- gA's drafts are gone, with nothing recording that", ) # A batch with no structured-output request clears the payload entirely and # still overwrites req_ids. get_draft_tokens then returns all -1 for a set of # requests it was never asked about. handler.set_draft_tokens(batch(["p1", "p2"], False), drafts_b) got = handler.get_draft_tokens() all_minus_one = all(all(t == -1 for t in row) for row in got.draft_token_ids) report( "a plain-only batch makes get_draft_tokens return all -1", all_minus_one, f"req_ids={got.req_ids} drafts={got.draft_token_ids}", ) print( " (utils.py comment claims this 'only happens when async " "scheduling is disabled')" ) # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Link B: a surviving -1 turns the mask fully permissive at real positions. # -------------------------------------------------------------------------- def link_b(): print("\nLink B -- surviving -1 makes grammar_bitmask fail OPEN") tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(TOKENIZER) vllm_config = VllmConfig( model_config=ModelConfig(tokenizer=TOKENIZER), structured_outputs_config=StructuredOutputsConfig(backend="xgrammar"), speculative_config=SpeculativeConfig( model="[ngram]", num_speculative_tokens=K ), ) manager = StructuredOutputManager(vllm_config) sampling_params = SamplingParams( structured_outputs=StructuredOutputsParams(json='{"type": "object"}') ) sampling_params.structured_outputs._backend = "xgrammar" sampling_params.update_from_generation_config({}, tokenizer.eos_token_id) prompt = tokenizer.encode('{"a"') request = Request( "req", prompt_token_ids=prompt, sampling_params=sampling_params, pooling_params=None, ) manager.grammar_init(request) while not request.structured_output_request._check_grammar_completion(): pass grammar = request.structured_output_request.grammar assert grammar.accept_tokens(request.request_id, prompt) # This is what the scheduler holds when the back-fill missed: the whole # window is still placeholders. window = [-1] * K bitmask = manager.grammar_bitmask( requests={request.request_id: request}, structured_output_request_ids=[request.request_id], scheduled_spec_decode_tokens={request.request_id: window}, ) assert bitmask is not None and bitmask.shape[0] == K + 1 row0_constrained = not (bitmask[0] == -1).all() report("row 0 is constrained (filled before the -1 is inspected)", row0_constrained) permissive = [i for i in range(1, K) if (bitmask[i] == -1).all()] report( "rows 1..K-1 are fully permissive", permissive == list(range(1, K)), f"rows {permissive} allow every token in the vocabulary", ) # And those rows are real sampling positions: the worker verifies the drafts # from its own GPU copy, so acceptance can walk into them. vocab = tokenizer.vocab_size row = bitmask[1] allowed = int(np.unpackbits(row.view(np.uint8), bitorder="little")[:vocab].sum()) report( "a permissive row allows the entire vocabulary", allowed == vocab, f"{allowed}/{vocab} token ids allowed at a position the model will sample", ) # Contrast: a fully back-filled window keeps every row constrained. Pick the # drafts from the grammar itself -- `validate_tokens` reports the accepted # prefix without advancing -- so this cannot fail on hand-picked token ids # that simply are not legal here. grammar.reset() assert grammar.accept_tokens(request.request_id, prompt) candidate = tokenizer.encode(':"b"')[:K] real = grammar.validate_tokens(list(candidate)) if not real: report("contrast: could not build a legal draft window", False, str(candidate)) else: bitmask2 = manager.grammar_bitmask( requests={request.request_id: request}, structured_output_request_ids=[request.request_id], scheduled_spec_decode_tokens={request.request_id: real}, ) any_permissive = [ i for i in range(bitmask2.shape[0]) if (bitmask2[i] == -1).all() ] report( "with real drafts, no row is permissive", not any_permissive, f"window of {len(real)} real drafts, permissive rows: {any_permissive}", ) def main(): print(f"vLLM under test: {__import__('vllm').__version__}") link_a() link_b() print() if ok: print("BUG REPRODUCED on stock main: the draft hand-off carries no") print("identity, so a request loses its drafts silently, and the grammar") print("bitmask then fails OPEN at real sampling positions.") return 1 print("at least one link no longer holds -- bug not reproduced here") return 0 if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main()) ```
Output on `main` @ `87b9b5b`: ``` vLLM under test: 0.28.1rc1.dev118+g87b9b5b8d Link A -- DraftTokensHandler keeps one unidentified slot [yes] drafts for 'gA' are available right after its own batch req_ids=['gA', 'pA'] [yes] after another batch runs, 'gA' can no longer be found req_ids=['gB', 'pB'] -- gA's drafts are gone, with nothing recording that [yes] a plain-only batch makes get_draft_tokens return all -1 req_ids=['p1', 'p2'] drafts=[[-1, -1, -1, -1], [-1, -1, -1, -1]] (utils.py comment claims this 'only happens when async scheduling is disabled') Link B -- surviving -1 makes grammar_bitmask fail OPEN [yes] row 0 is constrained (filled before the -1 is inspected) [yes] rows 1..K-1 are fully permissive rows [1, 2, 3] allow every token in the vocabulary [yes] a permissive row allows the entire vocabulary 50257/50257 token ids allowed at a position the model will sample [yes] with real drafts, no row is permissive window of 3 real drafts, permissive rows: [] BUG REPRODUCED on stock main: the draft hand-off carries no identity, so a request loses its drafts silently, and the grammar bitmask then fails OPEN at real sampling positions. ``` ### Reachability: why this is latent upstream today The end-to-end symptom needs `pipeline_parallel_size >= 2`, and that is currently unreachable for any small public checkpoint: - `create_draft_parallel_config` copies the target's pp_size to the drafter verbatim (`vllm/config/speculative.py:1647`), and `verify_with_parallel_config` then rejects any drafter that does not implement `SupportsPP`. - Of the registered draft heads, only `Glm4MoeLiteMTP` and `BailingMoeV3MTPModel` implement it. `Eagle3LlamaForCausalLM`, `MiMoMTP`, `DeepSeekMTP` and `DeepSeekV4MTP` do not. - Relaxing that gate is not sufficient either: with the check bypassed, `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` + `RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3` at `pp=2` fails while *constructing* the drafter on a non-last rank (`llama_eagle3.py:166` → `llama.py:282`). We hit the symptom in production because our deployment carries a local relaxation for a side-model drafter (a DSpark head, which runs on the last stage rather than being partitioned across stages) plus the PP plumbing to broadcast draft tokens between stages. Any upstream change that makes a side-model drafter work under PP — which seems a natural thing to want — turns this from latent into live. ### Field evidence (from that deployment) 2 nodes x 2 GPUs, `pipeline_parallel_size=2`, `tensor_parallel_size=2`, DeepSeek-V4-Flash with `dspark` K=7, xgrammar backend. | probe | result | |---|---| | `tool_choice=required`, solo into an idle engine | passes 3/3 | | `tool_choice=required`, one other grammar request decoding | **fails 3/3** | | `json_schema` | **fails** | | `tool_choice=auto`, `json_object`, plain text | passes (permissive grammar hides it) | | `temperature=0` | passes (the resample kernel returns early on the masked argmax) | | speculative decoding disabled | passes | Permissive grammars pass because an unconstrained token is usually still legal, which is why this presents for a long time as "one agent out of six occasionally emits garbage" rather than as a hard error. Instrumenting `update_draft_token_ids_in_output` to classify each structured-output request in the deferred `SchedulerOutput` (6 concurrent `tool_choice=required` requests, 2400+ deferred steps): ``` MISSING (absent from draft_token_ids.req_ids) 100% ALL_MINUS1 (present, all drafts -1) 0% REAL ~0% ``` Retaining the last 4 snapshots and reporting at what depth the request's drafts would have been found: ``` MISSING@depth1 == MISSING 100% ``` The drafts are never actually unavailable — they are exactly one snapshot away, 100% of the time, which is the signature of a single slot under alternating PP microbatches. Solo, the back-fill succeeds ~85% of the time, which is why this only shows up under concurrency. Histogram of where the first `-1` lands in the K=7 window, same load: ``` first -1 at index -> {0: 2710, 1: 6, 2: 4, 3: 3, 4: 4, 5: 21, 6: 12, 7: 1309} ``` 66% of grammar rows had no usable draft at all, i.e. rows 1..7 permissive. ### Relationship to #44006 #44006 made the **bonus** row stay constrained after `-1` padding, and `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py:144` asserts exactly that: ```python assert not (bitmask[-1] == -1).all() ``` Rows `1..K-1` are deliberately left permissive, on the assumption that a `-1` means "this draft was rejected by `validate_tokens`, so the sampler will reject it too". That assumption is sound when the `-1` really is a rejection signal. It is violated here, where `-1` means "the drafts never reached the scheduler" — and no test covers those rows. `rejection_sampler_utils.py:767` already resamples a `-1` position straight from the target distribution and needs no change. ### Suggested fix Two independent pieces; the first is the correctness fix and stands alone. 1. **Fail closed.** When a structured-output request's scheduled spec tokens still contain `-1` at index `j`, mark drafts `j..K-1` invalid (`is_valid_draft = draft_sampled >= 0`) so the accepted length cannot run past the last row with a real mask. Rows `0..j` are correctly masked, so row `j` still supplies the step's token under the right constraint. Cost: that step gets no speculative speed-up. 2. **Give the hand-off an identity.** Snapshot `req_states.draft_tokens` where `prepare_inputs` feeds it into `input_ids` — at *consumption* time, not proposal time — tagged with the scheduler's step counter, and retain the last few. The scheduler then asks for the snapshot belonging to the step it is sampling, by equality, instead of taking whatever ran last. A miss falls back to (1), so the failure mode is the conservative one rather than a wrong mask. Both are implemented and running in our deployment. Measured effect of (2) on top of (1), 5 concurrent requests, aggregate decode throughput: | grammar + plain | (1) only | (1)+(2) | |---|---|---| | 1 + 4 | 235.6 | 256.0 | | 3 + 2 | 170.7 | 260.2 | | 5 + 0 | 111.9 | **276.8** | With (2), grammar requests decode at 52–58 tok/s against a 52.5 tok/s plain-text baseline — the speculative speed-up is fully recovered. Back-fill hit rate goes to 100%, and bitmask rows carrying a real mask from 32% to 96.5%. Happy to open PRs for both if this looks like the right direction. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Searched existing issues and asked the documentation chatbot.
